# SlimDash

![SlimDash][banner]

Give a second life to old tablets, phones and e-readers: SlimDash shows your Home Assistant
dashboards as an ultra-light HTML page that even very old browsers can display smoothly
(Android 4.4 stock browser, iOS 7–12 Safari, Kindle…).

![Supports aarch64][aarch64-shield] ![Supports amd64][amd64-shield]

## Why

We all have an old phone or tablet sitting in a drawer, outdated or worn out. It has become too
slow for everyday use and can no longer keep up with the modern web or apps such as the Home
Assistant Companion app, yet we would rather give it a second life than throw it away.

The Home Assistant frontend needs a recent browser. On an old device it is slow, blank or
crashes. SlimDash renders the dashboard on the server and sends a page of a few kilobytes,
updated live, that keeps the layout of your original dashboard.

## Features

- **Your own dashboards**: reuses the views you already built in Home Assistant (sections,
  sizes, themes, icons, state labels in your language). Nothing to redesign. You can also build
  a dashboard (or view) made for each device — fewer cards, larger buttons, a light theme for an
  e-reader — and publish each one under its own address.
- **Live updates**: one WebSocket connection to Home Assistant, subscribed only to the
  entities on screen; the device receives a few bytes per change.
- **Actions**: toggle lights and switches, press buttons, run scripts and scenes, set
  light brightness, color and temperature, move covers, change values, switch views.
- **Three rendering types**, chosen automatically from the browser: type 1 for the oldest
  devices (Android 4.4, iOS 7–9), type 2 for 2016–2019 browsers, type 3 for recent ones.
- **Cameras**: snapshots refreshed every second, faster with Frigate, live video on recent
  devices.
- **Popular custom cards**: Mushroom, Bubble Card, button-card, stack-in-card, digital
  clock, Météo-France and more. Their main options are supported, not all of them: the aim is
  to stay simple and light, so advanced styling and scripted options are left out.
- **Light on your server and your network**: pages are rendered once and cached; no long-lived
  token needed.
- **Access control**: allowed networks and an optional access key.
- **Optional screen wake lock**: supported browsers can keep the display awake after the first touch or click; this requires Wake Lock API support and, where enforced, HTTPS.

## Tip

**Before installing SlimDash, debloat your devices to make them fast and smooth!**

## Warning

**Use these old devices at your own risk!** An old device comes with a few risks:

- **Battery overheating**: a worn-out battery left on charge all day can heat up and swell.
- **Network security**: an old system no longer gets security updates and relies on outdated
  certificates. Its known flaws come with it onto your local network.
- **Plain HTTP pages**: the access key travels unencrypted on your network. Keep
  `allowed_networks` limited to your devices and never open port 8099 to the Internet.
- **Sensitive controls**: anyone standing in front of the device can use what the dashboard
  shows. Avoid locks, alarm or garage door on a screen left in free access.

I strongly recommend managing the device's charging, isolating the device on your network and
blocking its access to the Internet. A few more good habits:

- Check the device now and then for a swelling battery. If the battery can be removed, you can
  power the device directly; a smart plug driven by Home Assistant can keep the charge between
  20 % and 80 %.
- Keep the device dedicated: no personal accounts (Google, mail) and no apps you do not need.

A separate standalone Docker deployment is available in the development fork; see its repository-level `docker/README.md` for details.

See the **Documentation** tab for setup and options.
